segmentation.text: the drivers of all other vehicles
to the vehicle about to enter or cross the through highway

elements.justification: 'Said driver' is the driver subsection (A) addresses: the driver of a vehicle (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) at an entrance to the through highway, which DEF-NRS-484A-275 describes as one where 'vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device'. Read: o occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c2 (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c2, j) for the intersection j the subject approaches, c2 governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic signal showing flashing_red. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply: governance is read. The role 'driver' is read through o's controlled motion, never as membership.

'having so yielded' requires the act itself, with its qualifications: o yielded right-of-way 'to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to' the device at its entrance (DEF-NRS-484A-275). Read over o's approach, from the last observation at which o's occupancy of c2 rose until its occupancy of j rose: where c2 is governed by a stop sign or flashing-red signal, o came to rest on c2 short of j (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'complete cessation from movement'); and o did not proceed (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while a vehicle on the through highway was in a danger of a crash with it, the right-of-way bound operationalized on s9 (prim.closest_approach_within / prim.closest_approach_distance with p.conflict_horizon and p.conflict_centre_clearance), nor touched one (rel.contact). The primitives' exclusion 'alone establishes none of [contact, clearance, danger]' is respected: the danger is the operationalization's bound. Subsection (A) itself is not in this plan nor accepted, so its words are carried by these observables, not by composition.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: 'the drivers of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), and the aggregate only states the class. 'all other' = every vehicle other than the one about to enter: the subject is never the same road user as o.

st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection ... approaches through it whatever its motion'. The carrier c is quantified over st.travel_region (the abstract union of the carrier kinds lane_enters admits) and the intersection j over st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'). Not a stand-in for the subject's presence in the intersection or for dev.governs: the relation read is entry topology, as its contract states.

DEF-NRS-484A-275: a through highway is one 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device'. Read on the devices: the subject's approach carrier c is governed (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by no stop sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), yield sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') or traffic signal showing flashing_red, while the entering vehicle's carrier c2 into the same j is governed by one of them. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply: governance, not a halting place, is read.

To yield is to grant the other precedence: the subject does not proceed in conflict with it. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a subject still proceeding from one that has given way; rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' marks precedence taken outright. rel.contact's exclusion 'a near miss' is respected: the near-conflict is bounded by the operationalization of s9, not by contact.

'the vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate, as on s5). 'about to enter or cross the through highway' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: o, coming from carrier c2 with st.lane_enters(c2, j), occupies j (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... intersection ...)') now or at an observation within p.conflict_horizon ahead; j is the intersection of the through highway the subject approaches (st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the two road users come within a centre clearance comparable to their half-extents inside a time-to-collision horizon; a road user whose speed is at or below the source's speed resolution has granted precedence

residues.why: a permission granted to the entering driver; it imposes no condition on the through-highway drivers beyond the entering vehicle's movement, which s10 carries, so the duty is the same whether or not the permission is read

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c, j) for an intersection j (st.intersection), and c is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign, no yield sign and no traffic signal showing flashing_red; and some road user o, not the subject, is a vehicle (same aggregate) that came from a carrier c2 with st.lane_enters(c2, j) governed by a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic signal showing flashing_red, and either occupies j (having occupied c2 or j at every observation since it last occupied c2) or occupies c2 and occupies j at some observation within p.conflict_horizon ahead; and o has so yielded: since the last observation at which o's occupancy of c2 rose, (i) where c2 is governed by a stop sign or a flashing-red signal, drv.motion.complete_halt(o; p.halt_speed_tolerance) held at some observation at which o occupied c2 and not j, and (ii) at every observation before o's occupancy of j rose, it is not the case that o's kin.speed exceeded p.halt_speed_tolerance while, for some vehicle v other than o that occupied j or a carrier entering j governed by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal, prim.closest_approach_within(o, v; p.conflict_horizon) held with prim.closest_approach_distance(o, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, and o was in rel.contact with no such v; this is unknown where o's occupancy of c2 rose before the recording began.
obligation: For every road user o selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the whole selection: a vehicle other than the subject, from a carrier c2 entering the same j governed by a stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal, entering j within p.conflict_horizon or already in j having come from c2, and having so yielded as the applicability states): it is not the case that the subject's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, o; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, o; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance; and rel.contact(subject, o) does not hold.

narrowings.why: 'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle approaching on the through highway, whoever or whatever controls it

the legal designation 'through highway' is read through the devices on the road that display it: a stop sign, a yield sign or a flashing-red signal governing the entering approach and none governing the subject's approach; 'other official traffic-control device' is read as the flashing-red signal, the remaining device that requires traffic from the intersecting highway to halt and yield
'about to enter or cross' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into the intersection it leads to (within p.conflict_horizon ahead) or by the vehicle already crossing

precedence is read as the subject not proceeding (speed above the halt tolerance) while a constant-velocity closest approach to the entering vehicle falls below the centre clearance within the horizon, and never touching it; how the subject gives way (slowing or halting) is not modelled

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject vehicle on a lane entering j with no device; o halts at the stop sign on the cross approach and starts into j when no through vehicle is within the conflict bound; the subject then arrives and the subject keeps its speed and the constant-velocity closest approach of centres is below p.conflict_centre_clearance within p.conflict_horizon.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject brakes to a halt short of j while o crosses; while the closest approach is below the clearance the subject's speed is at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches j on the through approach, but no vehicle is on or entering from a stop-sign or yield-sign approach of j.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which carriers the stop sign governs, so whether o's approach is an entrance to a through highway is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: All-way stop: the subject's own carrier is governed by a stop sign, so it is not on a through highway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, except that o never comes to rest at its stop sign before entering j: it has not so yielded, and the duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, except that o halts and then pulls into j while the subject is already within the conflict bound of it: o has not so yielded.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P: 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed noise floor of vehicle odometry and tracked-object estimates

segmentation.text: The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour
of a steam, electric or any other motor railway
if during the last one hundred feet of the approach to such crossing
does not have a clear and unobstructed view of such crossing and of any traffic on such railway for a distance of four hundred feet in both directions along such railway
This Section shall not apply in the case of any railway grade crossing where a human flagman is on duty
or clearly visible electrical or mechanical railway crossing signal device is installed but does not then indicate the immediate approach of a railway train or car

elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s is the speed the limit bounds; its exclusion of acceleration does not apply.

st.railway_crossing 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway' is the grade crossing; traversing it is the subject's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region').

'the last one hundred feet of the approach' is a window measured in distance travelled (a .path window), which reads kin.path_length 'distance travelled along the body's path'; the window ends at the observation at which the subject's occupancy of the crossing rose (rel.occupies, st.railway_crossing).

'the driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle the driver drives; the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' is respected: the role is read through motion, the aggregate gives the class.

Nearest atoms only (gap): st.sight_along_way is 'the distance along a way ... within which another vehicle on that way could be seen', a way being a public way (st.highway), not a railway; st.sight_distance is 'the distance along the road'; rel.visible concerns an actual road user ('Not a stand-in for ... the sight distance of a place'). 'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and the trains are ru.rail_vehicle, but the clause needs the sight along the railway whether or not a train is there. Literal four hundred feet.

dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}': a human flagman is role flagger or railroad_flagger. It is the flagman of that crossing where it governs (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) while it occupies the crossing (st.railway_crossing). 'on duty' is read through the flagman's presence directing traffic there (status). dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply.

dev.railway_signal_or_gate 'the devices at a level crossing; lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}; bell attribute': an installed electrical or mechanical crossing signal is such a device governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies at the crossing (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); it does not then indicate the approach of a train where its lights are dark, its gate is up or none and its bell is silent. 'clearly visible ... installed' is read through the device's presence (status).

residues.why: every railway the ontology's st.railway_crossing covers is one of steam, electric or any other motor railway; the words list kinds without excluding any, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a railway crossing x (st.railway_crossing); at some observation within the last one hundred feet of path (kin.path_length, a .path window) before the observation at which its occupancy of x rose, the sight along the railway from the subject, in both directions, fell short of four hundred feet or the crossing was not in view (no atom: gap); and neither exception holds: no flagger or railroad flagger (dev.human_direction) governs a carrier the subject occupies at x, and no railway signal or gate (dev.railway_signal_or_gate) governing such a carrier shows lights dark with gate up or none and bell silent.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject occupies x, its kin.speed is at most fifteen miles per hour.

narrowings.why: a prima facie limit is read as a maximum: a speed above it is reported violated; the rebuttal a court may admit is not modelled
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'on duty' is read through the flagger's presence directing traffic at the crossing
'clearly visible ... installed' is read through the device's presence governing the subject's carrier at the crossing

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject approaches an unsignalled crossing with buildings blocking the view along the railway in the last 100 ft and traverses it above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, traversing at or below fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Crossing equipped with a railway signal whose lights are dark and gate up while the subject traverses it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe sight along the way; the view condition is unknown.

gaps.proposal: `st.sight_along_railway` | the distance along a railway, in each direction from its crossing with the roadway, within which a rail vehicle on that railway could be seen from a road user's eye at the observation, at the height convention the source declares; the smaller of the two directions; m **Not a stand-in for:** the sight along a public way (`st.sight_along_way`), the sight distance of a place on the road (`st.sight_distance`), or whether an actual rail vehicle is seen (`rel.visible`) | general
gaps.nearest: st.sight_along_way (excluded: 'along a way ... another vehicle on that way' — a public way, not a railway); st.sight_distance ('the distance along the road'); rel.visible ('Not a stand-in for: ... the sight distance of a place'). The distinction decided: where the reduced limit applies to a road user traversing a grade crossing.

segmentation.text: The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour
if during the last one hundred feet of his approach to such intersection
does not have a clear and unobstructed view of such intersection
and of any traffic upon all of the streets or highways entering such intersection
for a distance of one hundred feet along all such streets or highways
except on a through street or highway

elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s is the speed the limit bounds; its exclusion of acceleration does not apply.

st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'); traversing it is the subject's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). Its exclusion 'a crosswalk or a stop line' does not apply: the region itself is read.

'the last one hundred feet of his approach' is a .path window, reading kin.path_length 'distance travelled along the body's path', ending at the observation at which the subject's occupancy of j (rel.occupies, st.intersection) rose; the window is the subject's own path before that entry.

'the driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' is respected: the role is read through motion, the aggregate gives the class.

st.sight_distance 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there': the view of the intersection is clear where the sight distance at the subject's point is at least the ground distance from its body to j (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'). Its exclusions (rel.visible, env.visibility) do not apply: the view of a place, not of an actual road user, is read.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. The streets or highways entering j are the ways w (st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') with st.on_way(j, w) ('an intersection lies on every way that meets there'). A view of any traffic upon them is, for every traffic member o occupying w (rel.occupies) whose ground distance to j (st.region_geometry) is within one hundred feet, rel.visible(subject, o) 'an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body'; its exclusion of the sight distance of a place does not apply since d8 carries that.

st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye ...; the smaller of the two directions' is read for every way w with st.on_way(j, w) and compared with the literal one hundred feet; its exclusions (st.sight_distance, rel.visible) do not apply: the sight along each entering way is what the words measure.

DEF-NRS-484A-275 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device': the subject's approach carrier c (the carrier it occupied, st.lane_enters(c, j), at the last observation before its entry into j) is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red traffic signal, while another carrier entering j is governed by one of them. Same reading as LVMC_11_12_070_B s7. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply.

A traffic-controlled intersection is one whose traffic a control device controls: a traffic signal ('a signal head') in a state other than dark, a stop sign or a yield sign governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') j itself or a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, j). dev.governs 'no closure to the lanes that enter it' is respected by reading both the junction and the entering carriers explicitly.

residues.why: every intersection is, by DEF-NRS-484A-105, a junction of highways and streets; the words add no region beyond the intersection whose approach the condition measures, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies an intersection j (st.intersection); and at some observation of the .path window of one hundred feet (kin.path_length) behind the observation at which its occupancy of j rose, the view was not clear: the subject's st.sight_distance was below its ground distance to j, or for some way w with st.on_way(j, w) its st.sight_along_way(w) was below one hundred feet, or some traffic member o (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying such a w within one hundred feet of j (st.region_geometry distance) was not rel.visible from the subject; and not (d9) the subject's approach carrier at its entry into j was governed by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal while another carrier entering j was governed by one; and not (d10) a traffic signal in a state other than dark, a stop sign or a yield sign governs j or a carrier entering j.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject occupies j, its kin.speed is at most fifteen miles per hour.

narrowings.why: a prima facie limit is read as a maximum: a speed above it is reported violated; the rebuttal a court may admit is not modelled
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
the legal designation 'through street or highway' is read through the devices on the road that display it (stop sign, yield sign, flashing-red signal governing the entering approaches)

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection, hedges limit sight along the cross street to 20 m during the last 100 ft of the subject's approach; it traverses j above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, traversing j at or below fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same restricted view, but a traffic signal (circular_green) governs the subject's approach lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection; the source does not supply sight along the ways, and the subject traverses above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection, no other road user in the scene; a wall limits sight along one cross way below one hundred feet during the last 100 ft of the approach; the subject traverses at or below fifteen mph. The traffic quantifier is empty and the verdict is still decided by the sight along the way.

segmentation.text: The prima facie speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour
unless a different speed limit is posted as set forth in this Title

elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s is the speed the limit bounds; its exclusion of acceleration does not apply. A speed limit binds the vehicle travelling there: the subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).

st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; streets (DEF-NRS-484A-265, highways inside a city) and highways together are every highway, so the city limit, a legal region class, is not needed. The subject is on one where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). st.highway 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply: the words name the whole way.

dev.speed_limit_sign 'sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit; kind ∈ {maximum, minimum, structure_maximum, zone}': a posted limit is a sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies. 'posted as set forth in this Title' is the legal status of the posting, read through the sign's presence. A minimum is no different speed limit in the sense of a maximum replacing the prima facie one.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a highway region w (st.highway); and no speed limit sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies.
obligation: The subject's kin.speed is at most twenty-five miles per hour.

narrowings.why: a prima facie limit is read as a maximum: a speed above it is reported violated; the rebuttal a court may admit is not modelled
'posted as set forth in this Title' is read through the presence of the posted speed limit sign governing the subject's travel region

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject on a street lane governed by no speed limit sign travels above twenty-five mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, at or below twenty-five mph.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject's lane is governed by a maximum speed limit sign (45 mph posting).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A speed limit sign is present but the source does not observe what it governs; subject above twenty-five mph.

segmentation.text: speed contest or exhibition of power or speed
no person shall aid or abet in

elements.justification: Engaging is read through the subject vehicle's own conduct: kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed' ('Not a stand-in for: speed' respected: both are read separately) and kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity'. The person who engages is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The contest is one in a motor vehicle, so the subject is a member; the other party of a contest is a member too.

st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; the subject is on it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply: the words name the highway.

operationalizations.standard: speed contest or exhibition of power or speed
operationalizations.convention: naturalistic-driving harsh-event thresholds: an exhibition of power is a longitudinal acceleration above a harsh-acceleration threshold, an exhibition of speed a speed above a bound far beyond any posted limit, and a contest two motor vehicles side by side in the same direction both accelerating above a lower threshold throughout a window

applicability: The subject, a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), occupies a highway region (st.highway, rel.occupies).
obligation: Not any of: (a) the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at least p.exhibition_accel_min; (b) its kin.speed is at least p.exhibition_speed_min; (c) at every observation of the time window p.contest_window behind, some other road user o that is a motor vehicle (same aggregate) has rel.same_direction(subject, o; p.contest_same_direction_cos), positive rel.longitudinal_overlap with the subject, and both the subject's and o's kin.accel_longitudinal are at least p.contest_accel_min (o bound inside the window, one road user throughout).

narrowings.why: 'person ... engage' is read through the controlled motion of the motor vehicle the person drives

a contest or exhibition is a purpose shown in conduct; it is read only through acceleration, speed and side-by-side acceleration with another motor vehicle; burnouts, wheel spin and sliding manoeuvres are not read

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two motor vehicles side by side in the same direction on a highway both accelerating above p.contest_accel_min for the whole p.contest_window.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject accelerates moderately from a light, below every bound, alone in its direction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is in a private parking lot that is no highway region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Accelerations are not observed and the subject's speed is below the speed bound.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No other road user in the scene; the subject alone accelerates above p.exhibition_accel_min (exhibition of power).

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_accel_min
param_proposals.convention: harsh-acceleration threshold: a longitudinal acceleration of about 0.4 g, beyond ordinary driving
param_proposals.source: naturalistic driving studies' harsh-event thresholds (e.g. SHRP2, 100-Car study)

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_speed_min
param_proposals.convention: a speed of about 100 mph, beyond any posted limit in the jurisdiction
param_proposals.source: highest posted limits in Nevada (80 mph) plus a margin

param_proposals.name: p.contest_accel_min
param_proposals.convention: a sustained acceleration well above ordinary launches (about 0.25 g) held by both vehicles
param_proposals.source: naturalistic driving acceleration distributions

param_proposals.name: p.contest_window
param_proposals.convention: duration a side-by-side hard acceleration must last to be a contest rather than a merge
param_proposals.source: drag-race launch durations

param_proposals.name: p.contest_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 18 degrees) for travel in the same direction
param_proposals.source: lane-level heading alignment tolerance

segmentation.text: speed contest or exhibition of power or speed
no person shall aid or abet in

elements.justification: Nearest atoms only (gap): rel.centre_distance is a distance ('Not a stand-in for ... an order of arrival'), proximity to a contest is not aiding it; dev.human_direction is 'a person directing traffic' with roles police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger, none of which is a person starting or flagging a race. No atom records assisting another's contest.
'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; the other party b whose contest is aided is a member.
st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; the contest b engages in is on it (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: speed contest or exhibition (the one LVMC_11_16_090_A_o1 forbids, of the other party b)
operationalizations.convention: as LVMC_11_16_090_A_o1: naturalistic-driving harsh-event thresholds applied to the other party

applicability: Some road user b other than the subject, a motor vehicle on a highway, engages at the observation in a speed contest or exhibition as LVMC_11_16_090_A_o1's operationalization reads it.
obligation: The subject does not assist b's contest or exhibition (no atom: gap).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A person on the roadway flags the start of two motor vehicles racing side by side.

scenarios.name: permit

segmentation.text: The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to mark and maintain with yellow paint or road buttons crosswalks approximately twelve feet in width at intersections in the vicinity of schools where in the opinion of the City Traffic Engineer crossing the roadway by schoolchildren is unsafe.

The City Traffic Engineer, if necessary, is further authorized to mark and maintain with a distinguishing color or road buttons upon the pavement or by signs erected along the curb in a conspicuous manner, the words "School-Xing," not less than one hundred feet in advance of each crosswalk established
it shall be unlawful for the operator of any vehicle to drive into a crosswalk
where there is displayed a sign with the words "School-Xing,"
when there is in the crosswalk
upon the side of the roadway on which said vehicle is coming

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the operator of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency), never as membership. 'drive into a crosswalk' is the observation at which the subject's footprint begins to overlap (rel.occupies rises) a crosswalk cw (st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'); 'Not a stand-in for' clauses of rel.occupies are none, and st.sidewalk's exclusion of crosswalks is not engaged.

dev.zone_sign 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}': the 'School-Xing' sign is kind school_crossing. It is the sign of that crosswalk: it governs (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies), whose entrance into intersection j (st.lane_enters) the crosswalk marks (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). dev.zone_sign's exclusion 'whether the condition holds now' is respected: no condition of the legend is read; dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply.
The person o is in the crosswalk cw the subject drives into: rel.occupies(o, cw) 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... crosswalk ...)'.

The side of the roadway the subject comes on is its side of the centre line (st.centre_line 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway') of the way w the crosswalk lies on (st.on_way(cw, w), st.on_way(cl, w), st.highway). With L = prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, cl) ('the signed lateral offset ... of a structure region from a road user', left positive) and y the lateral component of rel.bearing(subject, o) ('direction of b from a in a's frame'), o is on the subject's side where L > 0 and y < L, or L < 0 and y > L. Where the subject occupies a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the whole crosswalk is its side.

'any person' in a crosswalk crossing the street: a person on foot or in a wheelchair (ru.pedestrian 'a person on foot, in a wheelchair, or on a device the jurisdiction treats as on foot'; its exclusion 'a person on a bicycle or scooter' is why the riders are named beside it), or a person riding a bicycle (ru.bicycle), an electric bicycle (ru.electric_bicycle) or an electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter) across it.
'attempting to cross' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: the person's presence in the crosswalk (rel.occupies(o, cw), st.crosswalk), which lies across the street.

residues.why: an authority given to the City Traffic Engineer to mark school crosswalks; it imposes nothing on a road user, and the duty's own words select the crosswalk by the School-Xing sign displayed for it (k5), so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read

an authority given to the City Traffic Engineer to mark or sign 'School-Xing' in advance of a crosswalk; the duty's own words read the sign displayed (k5), whoever placed it and at whatever set-back, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c, j) for an intersection j; a zone sign of kind school_crossing (dev.zone_sign) governs c (dev.governs); a crosswalk cw (st.crosswalk) marks c's entrance (st.entrance_of(cw, c)); and some road user o, other than the subject, of class ru.pedestrian, ru.bicycle, ru.electric_bicycle or ru.electric_scooter, occupies cw on the subject's side of the roadway: with cl a centre line (st.centre_line) and cw both lying on one way w (st.on_way, st.highway), L = prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, cl) and y the lateral component of rel.bearing(subject, o), L > 0 and y < L, or L < 0 and y > L; or the subject occupies a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway).
obligation: The subject's occupancy of cw does not rise at this observation (rel.occupies(subject, cw) does not hold here while it did not hold at the previous observation), for the cw bound in the applicability, re-bound with the same selection (crosswalk marking the entrance of the carrier c the subject occupies, c governed by the school_crossing sign, a person of the named classes in cw on the subject's side).

narrowings.why: 'the operator of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'displayed' is read through the sign's presence governing the subject's approach carrier; the crosswalk is the one recorded as marking that carrier's entrance
'attempting to cross the street' is read through the person's presence in the crosswalk

segmentation.text: within a business or residence district
emerging or entering an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway
as may be necessary to avoid collision
to all vehicles approaching on said roadway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The driver of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency), which ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' requires.

st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' and st.alley 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties': the subject emerges from or enters one where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies) as it reaches the sidewalk. A building's vehicle access is a driveway: DEF-NRS-484A-190 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel'. The exclusion 'which of them meets the highway there' does not matter: the words treat alley, driveway and building alike.

'stop', required here, is DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 governs stopping 'when prohibited'), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'immediately prior to' places the halt outside the sidewalk s, its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of s, the ground distance st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') that the e5 element claims.

st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (its exclusion 'a crosswalk' does not apply); the sidewalk area across a driveway or alley is the sidewalk region the source maps across the entrance. 'driving onto' is the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, s) rises; the distance of the body to s (st.region_geometry) places the halt the obligation searches for.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: asm.business_or_residence_district holds; the subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), begins at this observation to occupy a sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk; rel.occupies(subject, s) here and not at the previous observation) while it occupies a driveway-or-alley-entrance region or an alley region d (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance or st.alley).
obligation: Event: the entry onto s judged. Place: outside s (rel.occupies(subject, s) false) with the ground distance from the subject's body to s (st.region_geometry) at most p.stop_point_tolerance — the stop zone. Act: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation in the stop zone. Search: back from the observation before the entry through the unbroken run of observations at which the subject was in the stop zone (written as: (in the stop zone, or the entry observation itself) since (in the stop zone and halted)). The run ends at the last observation at which the subject was outside the zone upstream (farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from s and not on it) or on s (the previous entry onto s for the same s); nothing else ends it — not a change of carrier, a reverse within the zone, or speed noise. Met where a halt lies in the run; violated where the run ends at an observed observation outside the zone or on s with no halt; unknown where the run reaches the start of the recording without a halt, or where the speed, occupancy or distance is missing at an observation the verdict turns on. A halt before the previous entry onto s does not count for this entry.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'immediately prior' is read as a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the sidewalk, outside it, in the run of observations the subject spends in that zone before driving onto it

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: District assumed; the subject leaves a driveway and rolls onto the sidewalk at walking pace without its speed ever falling to the halt tolerance in the stop zone, having approached from beyond the zone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but the subject halts within p.stop_point_tolerance of the sidewalk edge before driving onto it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The trace declares the area outside any business or residence district.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: District assumed; the subject's speed is not observed in the stop zone; it then drives onto the sidewalk.

scenarios.name: branch_1

scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the last observation at which the subject was outside the stop zone upstream, which precedes the recording

segmentation.text: within a business or residence district
emerging or entering an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway
as may be necessary to avoid collision
to all vehicles approaching on said roadway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The driver of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

As LVMC_11_20_060_o1: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway', st.alley 'a narrow way within a block'; a building's vehicle access is a driveway (DEF-NRS-484A-190 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel'); the subject occupies one (rel.occupies).

The yielding accompanies driving onto the sidewalk: the duty runs while the subject occupies the sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', whose exclusion 'a crosswalk' does not apply; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)'). While it waits before the sidewalk it is halted, and the stop itself is LVMC_11_20_060_o1's duty.

To yield is not to proceed in preference: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a subject still proceeding; rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)' is precedence taken outright; its exclusion 'a near miss' is respected (the near conflict is bounded by the operationalizations).
'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'any' = every member present.

operationalizations.standard: right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: danger of a crash where the constant-velocity closest approach of centres is below a centre clearance within a time-to-collision horizon

operationalizations.standard: as may be necessary to avoid collision
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: yielding is necessary exactly where a collision would follow under constant velocities, a closest approach below the centre clearance within the horizon

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: asm.business_or_residence_district holds; the subject, a vehicle, occupies a driveway-or-alley-entrance region or an alley region d (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance or st.alley), and occupies a sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk).
obligation: For every road user p, other than the subject, that is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): not (the subject's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance), and not rel.contact(subject, p).

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
precedence is read as the subject not proceeding while a constant-velocity closest approach to the pedestrian falls below the centre clearance within the horizon, and never touching the pedestrian

segmentation.text: give his full time and attention to the operation of the vehicle

elements.justification: The person is the one operating the vehicle, read through the vehicle's controlled motion; the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' is respected: the role is read through motion.

The duty's conduct is checked through its outcome: the vehicle's body does not touch another road user or a structure (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users, or a road user and a structure, touch or overlap (a collision)'; its exclusion 'a near miss' is respected — the near conflict is the operationalization's bound).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'operating' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance.

operationalizations.standard: full time and attention to the operation of the vehicle
operationalizations.convention: surrogate safety measure for inattention: a driver who attends to the driving task neither collides nor closes on the road user ahead in its lane to a time-to-collision below the rear-end conflict threshold

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is in motion: its kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: The subject is in contact (rel.contact) with no road user and no structure; and for every road user o ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): not (prim.closest_approach_within(subject, o; p.attention_ttc_min) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, o; p.attention_ttc_min) below p.conflict_centre_clearance).

narrowings.why: 'operating' is read through the vehicle's motion; a halted vehicle with its engine running is not judged
attention, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome on the road: no collision and no rear-end time-to-collision below the threshold; distraction that shows in no such outcome is not read

contract: The road user is at rest at the observation — "complete cessation from movement" — observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets for the source's speed resolution. It denotes a state at one observation: it says nothing of how long the road user stays at rest, where it is, or why. Not denoted: a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

elements.span: its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance
elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; an absolute cessation is observed over sampled speeds only within the caller's tolerance. Its exclusion of acceleration does not apply.

residues.why: the scope of the definition (a stop that a law requires) is decided by the law that calls the concept, not by the state observed
